What would be INVALID (a wealth-level soft restart), analysed because the name invites it. Suppose at a data-dependent time tau one replaced the wealth by W' = rho W_tau + (1 - rho) and continued with the same factors. Then W'_t = rho M_t + (1-rho) M_t / M_tau after tau. If M_{tau-1} < 1 the jump E[W'_tau | H_{tau-1}] = rho E[M_tau|H_{tau-1}] + 1 - rho can exceed M_{tau-1} (e.g. M_{tau-1} = 0.5, rho = 0.5 gives up to 0.75): the process is not a supermartingale and Ville fails. The mechanism is that the capital "1 - rho" is injected from nowhere. The valid version is a start-time mixture with a capital ledger: weights w_j that are H_{j-1}-measurable (adaptive is fine), with sum_j w_j <= 1 pathwise, wealth W_t = sum_{j<=t} w_j prod_{s=j+1}^t f_s + (1 - sum_{j<=t} w_j). The empirical-Bernstein gate tests the *average expected net gain over the fixed monitor horizon*, a different null from the sequential test's eventwise conditional-mean null. It maps bounded gains `G_t in [-B,B]` to `U_t=(G_t+B)/(2B) in [0,1]`. Let `s_n^2` be the unbiased sample variance and split candidate level `alpha_i` equally between variance estimation and the upper-tail bound: `delta_v=delta_m=alpha_i/2`. For independent observations, including non-identically distributed observations, the empirical variance bound gives `sqrt(v_bar) <= sqrt(s_n^2)+sqrt(2 log(1/delta_v)/(n-1))` with probability at least `1-delta_v`; `v_bar` is the average marginal variance. Bernstein's inequality then bounds `U_bar - E[U_bar]` by `sqrt(2 v_bar log(1/delta_m)/n)+log(1/delta_m)/(3n)`. The gate promotes only if the observed mean exceeds the null boundary `1/2` plus this radius. Capping `v_bar` at `1/4` uses the known variance maximum for `[0,1]`. This is an established empirical-Bernstein construction, not a new theorem; see [Maurer and Pontil (2009), Theorems 10 and 11](https://www.cs.mcgill.ca/~colt2009/papers/012.pdf). It is valid for the grid's independent synthetic monitor draws, even where a deterministic regime schedule makes their distributions differ over time. It is invalid under unmodeled serial dependence or feedback that couples outcomes across events. The base Hoeffding gate instead uses only boundedness and the conditional-mean null, so it remains the dependence-robust fixed-horizon comparator.

The reduction behind the policy is elementary: couple a randomized all-positive terminal test to the same fixed cohort and stop buying labels after the first zero. On every potential label tape the terminal action is unchanged. Under the endpoint causal null, a promotion requires `m` successive positive queried labels, so its worst-case probability is at most `lambda 2^{-m}` when the entry lottery has mass `lambda`; here `(m,lambda)=(3,4/5)`, giving `1/10`. Under any alternative label law, expected query count becomes `lambda sum_{j=0}^{m-1} P(Y_1=...=Y_j=1)`, with the empty-prefix probability equal to one. This is an exact cost-saving coupling for the all-positive test, not a new sequential-testing principle. Early futility stopping and cost-aware group-sequential testing have long prior art, including [Brown and Rutemiller (1971)](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.19.4.970), [Gould and Pecore (1982)](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/69.1.75), and delayed-response group-sequential testing by [Hampson and Jennison (2013)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9868.2012.01030.x). The finite optimum remains a mechanism diagnostic and matched baseline, not a scalable method. Historical promotion-risk control remains distinct from current-regime evidence and future utility after a reversal.

For an unbiased prediction-powered estimator `h(X)+I/q(X)(H-h(X))`, the conditional query-randomization variance is `(1/q(X)-1) v(X)`, where `v(X)=E[(H-h(X))^2|X]`. Under a fixed expected label budget and no propensity bounds, minimizing the integrated variance gives `q(X) proportional to sqrt(v(X))`; with lower and upper bounds, the solution is clipped at those bounds. Thus power 0.5 is the classical Neyman allocation baseline. Other powers are tuning candidates, not novel theory. The grid chooses the power minimizing the empirical validation estimate of this variance and measures its out-of-time performance without using monitor outcomes for selection.
